newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine to sell stakes in two regional power firms.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine to sell stakes in two regional power firms.

text.p: Ukraine's State Property Fund (FDM) said on Friday it planned to hold tenders in July for stakes in two large regional power companies.
Foreign investors will be able to participate in the investment tenders for 8.5 percent of Kievenergo and 27.43 percent of Zaporizhoblenergo, it said in a statement.
The winner of an investment tender is the bidder offering the most investment in the company, not the highest price for the stake.
The Ministry of Energy and Electrification would keep 51 percent of both companies.
The authorised capital of Kievenergo, which serves the Kiev region, is 27 million hryvnias, divided into 108.36 million shares with a face value of 00.25 hryvnias each.
Its pre-tax profit was 110,000 hryvnias in 1996.

The company employs 8,700 workers, entitled to a 30.5 percent stake in the firm. Managers are entitled to five percent, and five percent of shares were reserved for purchase by Ukrainians and companies holding privatisation certificates.

The authorised capital of Zaporizhoblenergo, serving the eastern Ukrainian region of Zaporizhya, is 44.8 million hryvnias and its 4.48 million shares have a face value of 00.10 hryvnias each. Its pre-tax profit last year was 64,490 hryvnias. Outstanding debts at the end of last year totalled 33 million hryvnias while the company is owed 29 million hryvnias.
Zaporizhoblenergo employs about 4,500 workers. Workers and and managers are entitled to a 21.57 percent stake in the company, the statement added.
The government approved last month a plan to privatise all 18 energy companies in Ukraine. ($1 = 1.841 hryvnias)
